679af6e7b3.q: What FP&A processes are most suitable for RPA automation and where do teams underestimate its potential?
679af6e7b3.a: Standard reporting is good for RPA because it is rule-based, repetitive, and has heavy transaction volumes—such as sending P&L reports, KPI dashboards, or preparing monthly management reports. However, teams underestimate that over-automation can desensitize information; critical reports that are the backbone of the business require human analyst review and stakeholder discussion to understand what the data tells you about financial health, not just automated report distribution.

a38b0564bf.q: How should finance teams prioritize which processes to automate first in FP&A transformation?
a38b0564bf.a: Prioritize using a matrix: quick wins have highest benefit with lowest complexity and should be done first since robots build quickly and generate highest benefits; must-do initiatives have highest benefit but high complexity so still execute them; low hanging fruit has lowest benefit and lowest complexity; long-term strategic initiatives have lowest benefit but highest complexity. For low-complexity tasks, operations teams can learn tools like UiPath or Microsoft Power Automation; for high-complexity initiatives, engage internal RPA teams, developers, or external consultants.
